literal: Good family having been born, in oneself blame him who shrinks from, even having given, acquiring is necessary friendship.
translation: Even by paying a price, one must acquire the friendship of a person born in a good family who shrinks from disgrace.
modern: நல்ல குடியில் பிறந்து தன்னிடம் பழி சேர்வதற்கு வெட்கப்படும் இயல்புடையவனின் நட்பை, ஏதேனும் விலை கொடுத்தாவது பெற்றுக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the immense value of befriending someone of noble character. The phrase 'குடி பிறந்து' refers to being born into a respectable family, which instills strong moral values. Such a person will naturally fear and avoid any 'பழி' (blame or disgrace) falling upon themselves ('தன்கண்'). The poet advises that the friendship ('நட்பு') of such a principled individual is so precious that one must acquire it ('கொளல் வேண்டும்') even if it means giving up something valuable in return ('கொடுத்தும்').
